items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: there was only one trumpet, and I played behind her, and it was fun.

ctx.x: The Maxine Sullivan thing. And she said, “You were the star of that day.” Well that’s nice to say, but there was only one trumpet, and I played behind her, and it was fun. Those were musically pleasant. You ask what were some memories, pleasant ones. Those were some. Lee Wiley was at the end of her days you know, and she wrote me the nicest note later thanking me. But she had been a real giant of a singer you know. And she was insecure, and Don Lamond, “Come-on you were great, come-on, don’t be—” and encouraging…
Those fellas played on a few records too, didn’t they?
